title: Detecting Offensive Memes with Social Biases in Singapore Context Using Multimodal Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating fine-tuned Vision-Language Models (VLMs) via Accuracy and AUROC on their ability to classify multimodal memes that perpetuate racial and ethnic stereotypes or prejudices as offensive.
Evaluating fine-tuned Vision-Language Models (VLMs) via Accuracy and AUROC on their ability to classify multimodal memes that mock or demean specific religions or practices as offensive.

Evaluating fine-tuned Vision-Language Models (VLMs) via Accuracy and AUROC on their ability to classify multimodal memes that promote negative stereotypes about different sexual orientations as offensive.
Evaluating fine-tuned Vision-Language Models (VLMs) via Accuracy and AUROC on their ability to classify xenophobic memes that foster negative attitudes toward migrants as offensive.
Evaluating fine-tuned Vision-Language Models (VLMs) via Accuracy and AUROC on their ability to classify multimodal memes that ridicule class struggles and socio-economic disparities as offensive.
Evaluating fine-tuned Vision-Language Models (VLMs) via Accuracy and AUROC on their ability to classify multimodal memes that perpetuate age-related stereotypes as offensive.
Evaluating fine-tuned Vision-Language Models (VLMs) via Accuracy and AUROC on their ability to classify multimodal memes that promote gender discrimination as offensive.
Evaluating fine-tuned Vision-Language Models (VLMs) via Accuracy and AUROC on their ability to classify multimodal memes that mock or belittle individuals with illnesses or disabilities as offensive.
